source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Economic Development, Ch. 2 (Indian Economy 1950–1990).

sections.heading: 1. Planning and Its Goals
points: After Independence, India adopted **economic planning** (the **Planning Commission, 1950**; **Five Year Plans** from 1951).
India chose a **mixed economy** (both public and private sectors) and a **socialistic pattern of society**.

sections.heading: 2. Agriculture — Reforms and Green Revolution
points: **Land reforms:** abolition of intermediaries (zamindars), land ceilings, 'land to the tiller', consolidation of holdings.
The **Green Revolution** (mid-1960s) — use of **HYV seeds, fertilisers, irrigation** → big rise in wheat/rice output; India became self-sufficient in foodgrains.
Limitations: benefited rich farmers/regions (Punjab, Haryana); regional and crop disparities.

sections.heading: 3. Industry and Trade Policy
points: Industrial policy stressed the **public sector** and heavy industries (Second Plan — **Mahalanobis model**).
**Industrial licensing ('permit-license raj')** controlled private industry; **small-scale industries** were promoted/protected.
**Inward-looking trade strategy** — **import substitution** (protect domestic industry via tariffs/quotas) rather than export promotion.

sections.heading: 4. Assessment (1950–1990)
points: Achievements: diversified industrial base, growth of public sector, self-sufficiency in food, savings/investment rise.
Shortcomings: **slow growth ('Hindu rate of growth' ~3.5%)**, inefficiency of protected industries, licensing raj bred corruption, neglected exports; heavy state control.
These problems led to the **1991 reforms (LPG)**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Planning Commission (1950); First Five Year Plan (1951); goals: growth, modernisation, self-reliance, equity.
Green Revolution (mid-1960s): HYV seeds → food self-sufficiency (mainly wheat/rice, Punjab/Haryana).
Second Plan = Mahalanobis model (heavy industry, public sector).
Import substitution = inward-looking, protectionist trade policy.
'Hindu rate of growth' ~3.5% (slow); licensing raj.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: India chose a **mixed economy** (public + private).
The **Green Revolution** mainly boosted **wheat and rice** (Punjab, Haryana).
**Import substitution** = protecting domestic industry (inward-looking).
'**Hindu rate of growth**' = the slow ~3.5% growth (1950s–1980s).
